# Abundance

> A primary-sourced arithmetic of what humanity already produces, divided by how many of us there are. For each essential resource with reliable global production data (food, water, electricity, output), the world total is divided by the UN mid-2024 population estimate and compared to a published minimum need. Every figure links to a primary source. Public domain (CC0 1.0) — take it, cite it, disprove it.

Claim under test: in 2026 the world produces enough food, water, electricity and output to meet every human's basic needs, so hunger, homelessness and energy poverty are distribution outcomes rather than production outcomes. This is a factual claim, not a political program. Limits are stated in the methodology.

Crawling and citation are welcome; see robots.txt. Numbers are recomputed in the browser from the JSON datasets below — cite the JSON, not the prose, when you want the underlying figure and its source.

## Core reading

- [Homepage](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/): editorial introduction, resource comparisons, guided reading index.
- [The full essay](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/essay.html): per-capita arithmetic for ~14 essentials, recomputed from cited data.
- [Open letter](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/letter.html): the case made to anyone who can act on it, cited throughout.
- [Course](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/course.html): structured reading path through the material.
- [Country case studies](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/case-studies.html): eleven nations that chose to lift underclass suffering, each with its counter-narrative.
- [By country](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/countries.html): 91 countries × 10 World Bank indicators.
- [Waste heat into drinking water](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/datacenter-water.html): datacenter cooling coupled to membrane distillation, with honest limits.

## Data (machine-readable, every entry cited)

- [essentials.json](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/data/essentials.json): food, water, electricity, GDP, wealth, military and health spending — the divisor set behind every per-capita figure.
- [pilots.json](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/data/pilots.json): cash-transfer programs with peer-reviewed or official evaluations (Kenya RCT, Alaska, Iran 2011, Stockton SEED, Finland, others).
- [case-studies.json](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/data/case-studies.json): country-scale precedents with primary sources and counter-narratives.
- [countries.json](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/data/countries.json): World Bank Open Data indicators per country (CC-BY-4.0), regenerated by scripts/build_countries.py.

## Method and evidence

- [methodology.md](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/methodology.md): how each number was derived, and what the arithmetic does not show.
- [bibliography.md](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/bibliography.md): ~100 academic references by topic.
- [Counterarguments](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/papers/counterarguments.md): a standing steelman of the strongest case against this project.
- [Cash-transfer evidence](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/papers/cash-transfer-evidence.md)
- [Inequality and wealth](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/papers/inequality-and-wealth.md)
- [Sen on entitlement](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/papers/sen-entitlement.md)
- [Historical context](https://lordbasilaiassistant-sudo.github.io/Abundance/papers/historical-context.md)
